D013-D009_h001.question:
I’ve been in a really dark place for about five months now. I cry in the car on the way to the lot and sometimes in my office with the door closed, for no real reason other than feeling completely useless. Everything I do feels slowed down — even walking across the showroom, picking up keys, talking to customers. The guys joke that I’m “moving like an old man.”  

My head just loops on every little mistake I’ve ever made — deals I botched, how I handled the divorce, times I snapped at my kid. I’ll lie in bed replaying this stuff for hours, telling myself I ruined everything. Sometimes, when I’m standing on a parking structure or waiting at a busy crosswalk, I get this strong urge to just step off or walk into traffic. I haven’t made a plan, but the impulse scares me. It’s gotten hard to keep the business running; I’m avoiding customers and missing follow-ups.  

What’s confusing is this isn’t how I’ve always been. I’ve had stretches in the past where I barely slept, felt on top of the world, talking fast, full of ideas, selling cars like crazy for weeks — people even told me I seemed “amped up” — but nothing like that during these past five months.
D013-D009_h001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
For about five months now I’ve felt like I’m stuck in this heavy, grey mood. I cry at my desk, in the bathroom, on the way home from the agency — over emails I think I messed up or a client sounding annoyed. I can’t seem to hold it in. I’m constantly on edge physically too; I can’t sit through a full meeting without bouncing my leg or picking at the skin around my nails until they bleed. At home I pace the apartment instead of relaxing.

I keep replaying tiny mistakes, like sending a draft late or forgetting to follow up, and I feel like I’m ruining campaigns, letting everyone down. It’s this crushing sense that I’m fundamentally bad and deserve whatever goes wrong. A lot of nights I just lie there thinking it would be easier if I didn’t wake up, not that I have a plan, more like I’m tired of existing.

This isn’t the first time my mood’s been off. Last year I had a stretch of about a week where I barely slept, felt insanely energized and “on,” talking nonstop, taking on way too many projects at work and socially, feeling almost invincible before crashing back down into this.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h003.question:

Most nights, when I finally collapse into bed, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but the idea of just…not existing anymore feels weirdly comforting.

This feels very different from times in the past when I’d suddenly have a ton of energy for days, barely sleep, talk a mile a minute on air and off, start all these projects and spend too much—those “up” times that everyone around me noticed before I crashed into stretches like this.

Sometimes, when I’m crossing the street or standing by the train platform, I get this sudden urge to just step out, like a pull. I scare myself.

What confuses me is that I’ve also had these other times—maybe a week or so—where I barely sleep, feel amazing, talk nonstop, take on extra clients, spend too much online, and feel unbeatable. Those bursts have happened a few times before this long down period.
